MI-2025-HB6443.title: Health facilities: hospitals; emergency medical screening and stabilizing treatment; require hospitals to provide. Amends 1978 PA 368 (MCL 333.1101 - 333.25211) by adding secs. 17028, 17528, 21528, 21528a, 21528b, 21528c & 21528d.

actions.text: introduced by Representative Rep. Carrie Rheingans
referred to Committee on Health Policy

MI-2025-HB6443.aiSummary: The bill would require hospitals to give an emergency medical screening and stabilizing treatment to people who ask for it or who appear to need urgent care. It would also require hospitals to keep a log of these cases, not ask about ability to pay before giving emergency care, and follow set rules before moving or discharging a patient who is not stable. The bill also sets duties for on-call physicians and bars them from making false statements about a patient’s condition or the transfer rules.

MI-2025-HB6436.title: Civil procedure: statute of limitations; statute of limitation for libel or slander; modify. Amends sec. 5805 of 1961 PA 236 (MCL 600.5805) & adds sec. 5819.

actions.text: introduced by Representative Rep. Kristian Grant

MI-2025-HB6436.aiSummary: The bill would change Michigan's time limit for filing libel or slander claims and would add a new rule for slander of title cases. A slander of title case would have to be filed within 3 years after the latest of when the false property claim is found, when a law enforcement investigation ends, or when any related criminal case is finished. It would affect people bringing these kinds of court cases in Michigan.

MI-2025-SB1026.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for Michigan domestic credit unions that use an assumed name, or a name other than their legal one. It would require notice to the state before using a new assumed name and let the state block or stop a name that is confusing or misleading. Credit unions using an assumed name would also have to show both names clearly in signs, ads, mailings, and key account papers.

MI-2025-HB6429.title: Environmental protection: solid waste; definition of coal combustion residuals; provide for. Amends, adds & repeals (See bill).

actions.text: introduced by Representative Rep. David Martin
referred to Committee on Natural Resources and Tourism

MI-2025-HB6429.aiSummary: The bill would change Michigan’s solid waste law to add a definition for coal combustion residuals, which are left over from burning coal, and set rules for how those materials can be used or handled. It also would update many related terms in the state’s environmental protection law, including several kinds of beneficial use, or allowed reuse, of ash and other waste materials.

MI-2025-SB265.aiSummary: The bill would require at least 1% of certain Michigan transportation funds to be spent on nonmotorized transportation, like bike and walking paths, and it would let that money be used for building, improving, maintaining, or repairing those facilities. It would also set rules for when these features must be added during road projects and for 5-year plans by the state, counties, cities, and villages that get this funding. Snow removal would not count as maintenance under this bill.

MI-2025-SB1208.title: Insurance: no-fault; election to opt out of PIP coverage; modify length of election. Amends sec. 3107d of 1956 PA 218 (MCL 500.3107d).

actions.text: REFERRED TO COMMITTEE ON FINANCE, INSURANCE, AND CONSUMER PROTECTION

MI-2025-SB1208.aiSummary: The bill would change how long a driver can keep an election to opt out of no-fault personal injury protection coverage. The election would stay in place while the person keeps insurance with the same insurer or an affiliate, unless the person revokes it in writing. If the person loses the required health coverage, they would have 30 days to get new coverage that includes that protection.

MI-2025-SB1201.title: Agriculture: other; Michigan animal agriculture alliance; establish. Amends 1988 PA 466 (MCL 287.701 - 287.746) by adding sec. 35.
MI-2025-SB1201.aiSummary: The bill would create a Michigan animal agriculture alliance to set up and run a grant program for animal research, working with the state agriculture department, Michigan State University, and industry representatives. It would also create a new animal research fund in the state treasury to hold and pay out grant money. The legislature would have to put at least $3 million into the fund each year, and any money left in the fund at the end of the year would stay there.

MI-2025-HB4301.aiSummary: Michigan has enacted a law that expands the definition of an authorized emergency vehicle. The law also changes which vehicles may use certain emergency lights, affecting fire, police, ambulance, and some rescue and aid vehicles.

MI-2025-SR141.title: A resolution to urge the federal government to report on the abduction of Ukrainian children by the Russian Federation and assist in their return.
MI-2025-SR141.aiSummary: Adopted by the Michigan Senate, this resolution asks the U.S. State Department to report on the abduction and military-style training of Ukrainian children by Russia. It also asks Congress to set aside money to help return the children to Ukraine. The resolution asks the U.S. government to make their return a priority in talks.
